body:
Opening a UI/UX design draws its screens: the row and column structure, sized as the design says, rendered with Lustre inside the Design page.

### Do

- Add a renderer in Lustre that takes a design's element tree and draws it. It holds the only mapping from layout properties to styles, so the format itself stays free of CSS.
- Every element it outputs carries `data-design-id` with the element's ID. Pointing depends on this later (feature:afd9fe8bae36c59c).
- A design with several screens shows all of them. Ask the human how they should be arranged before building this.
- Keep the renderer separate from the page's state, so proposals can draw through it later.

### Acceptance

- Tests: each layout property produces the expected output, nested containers draw in order, fill, hug and fixed each size correctly, and every drawn element carries its ID.
- A browser check that a nested layout looks right; say in the task note if it has to be manual.

### Left out

Components, theme and click-through behavior, which are the next tasks. Drawing keeps to elements that exist today.
title: ui: draw a screen's layout
